key_points: GDPNow for the current quarter jumped to ~5.0% from 1.5%, signalling growth reaccelerating well above potential.
FOMC statement and minutes describe solid expansion, strong productivity and AI capex with no sign of slowing; consumer sentiment rebounded from 49.5 to 55.2 and claims remain very low (197k).
Above-trend growth with a Fed openly considering hikes (3 hawkish dissents) supports modestly higher front-end and long-end yields and a firmer dollar; the curve effect is roughly neutral.
Strong earnings/AI-driven activity is supportive for equities, tighter HY spreads and a lower VIX; modestly supportive for oil demand.
Higher real-rate pressure from strong growth is a mild headwind for gold; the signal is kept modest because yields are already at 1-year highs and much growth strength appears priced.
Core PCE running ~3.3% y/y with June m/m ~0.14%; staff and participants see core changing little through year-end and upside risks to inflation, with broadening price pressures noted.
June headline CPI fell on post-Hormuz energy decline, but WTI rebounded ~22% in July, so the mid-August July CPI/PPI prints likely show a renewed energy-driven headline pickup.
Three hawkish dissents for a hike in July and removal of easing bias mean hot inflation prints transmit mostly to the front end: mild upward tilt for 2y > 10y, slight flattening bias in 2s10s.
10y breakevens at 2.28 (32nd pct) look low relative to an energy rebound and sticky core; modest upside tilt.
Hawkish-inflation repricing is a mild headwind for equities and credit spreads, mild support for USD and VIX; gold ambiguous between inflation hedge and higher real rates.
Yields already at 1y highs and much hawkishness priced, so tilts kept small.
Labor market is stable-to-firm: unemployment ticked down to 4.2%, initial claims at a very low 197k (vs 218k a year ago), FOMC describes job gains keeping pace with workforce.
Payroll gain of only +57k in June is soft, but with low labor-force growth it is consistent with a balanced market; no sign of loosening that would revive cut expectations.

With three hawkish dissents in July, a firm labor backdrop removes the employment-side argument for easing and keeps hike risk alive: mild upward bias to front-end yields, more than to 10y, implying slight bear-flattening of 2s10s.
Firm labor supports the dollar modestly via rate differentials and keeps credit spreads and VIX contained; equity effect roughly neutral (growth support offset by rate headwind).
July payrolls (early August) is the key near-term event; low claims tilt odds toward a non-weak print, but the signal is modest so probabilities stay close to 0.50.

The Fed's reaction function has turned hawkish. The July 29 hold drew 3 dissents (Hammack, Kashkari, Logan), all preferring a 25bp hike. The easing bias was dropped in June, and the statement now says 'The Committee will deliver price stability.'
June minutes: 'many' participants saw the appropriate rate above the current range by year-end. 'Most' saw firming as warranted if inflation stays elevated on AI demand, energy or tariffs.

The 2y at 4.28 is already about 65bp above the 3.625 mid of the funds range, so much tightening is priced. Even so, the risk of a September or October hike, or a hawkish September SEP dot shift, still exceeds what a one-hike-by-mid-2027 path implies. That gives a modest upward tilt to front-end yields.
Hawkish policy repricing concentrates at the front end, so the factor biases 2s10s toward flattening.
Policy-rate differentials favor the dollar versus AFEs. The ECB and BoE are also hiking, which limits the edge.
Tighter policy expectations weigh mildly on equities, gold and inflation breakevens, and push HY spreads and the VIX slightly up.
Offsetting the hawkish tilt: headline CPI fell in June on energy, which keeps the doves' 'supply shock fades' scenario alive, so the tilts stay modest.
August quarterly refunding (early August) and the following 3y/10y/30y auction week create near-term duration supply concession risk with 10y already at a 1y high.

Fed minutes flag a shift in Treasury ownership toward price-sensitive private holders and a rising term premium; the last week's bear steepening (10y +6bp, 2y -5bp) looks term-premium driven, favoring further 2s10s steepening from fiscal supply.
Bill-heavy financing is absorbed partly by Fed reserve-management bill purchases, so front-end (2y) gets little signal from supply; the effect concentrates in the long end.
Mid-September tax receipts lift the TGA and drain reserves modestly, a small headwind for risk assets and credit spreads over the 1-3 month horizon.

Fiscal/term-premium-driven yield rises tend to be mildly dollar-negative and gold-supportive (debasement narrative), and a mild headwind for equity valuations; oil and breakevens see little direct signal.
Financial conditions are loose: NFCI -0.55 (looser than a year ago), HY OAS 2.85% near the tight end, VIX ~16; equity-supportive backdrop persists absent a liquidity shock.

Reserves ample and money markets soft (repo traded below IORB in May); Fed reserve-management bill purchases are slowly growing the balance sheet and shrinking bill supply, a mild anchor for front-end yields.
Desk notes shift of Treasury ownership toward price-sensitive private investors, implying upward term-premium pressure on the 10y and a steeper 2s10s from the liquidity channel.
Private-credit stress (slowing BDC inflows, rising redemptions) and already-tight spreads skew HY spreads modestly wider over 1-3 months; spreads widened 10bp in the past month.
Ample dollar liquidity and Fed bill buying are mildly dollar-negative and mildly gold-supportive; oil and breakevens get little signal from this factor.
Signals are modest overall; no acute funding stress visible, so probabilities stay close to 0.50.
Dollar index specs net long at the 99th percentile (29.5% of OI) while the dollar is already slipping: crowded long, so the contrarian tilt is lower for the dollar.
10y T-note specs are net short at the 20th percentile with the 10y yield at a 1-year high (100th percentile). Short-covering risk tilts the 10y yield slightly lower.

2y specs are at their least-short level in a year (99th percentile), so there is little squeeze fuel at the front end. That leaves a neutral to slightly higher 2y yield, and the combination implies mild 2s10s flattening.

ES positioning is at the 97th percentile of the past year and VIX sits at 16 (23rd percentile) after a 2.6-point weekly drop. That points to complacency: VIX mean-reversion higher, a mild equity giveback and slight HY spread widening.
Gold positioning is at the 43rd percentile after a 14% three-month drop: washed out, giving a mild contrarian upside tilt.
Oil specs added 38k contracts while price fell 6%; positioning is mid-range (59th percentile), so no clear signal. Positioning gives no signal on breakevens either.
Foreign central banks (ECB already hiking, UK hike priced) are tilting hawkish into the energy shock, narrowing short-rate differentials versus a Fed on hold: mildly dollar-negative.
Speculative DX futures longs sit at the 99th percentile of 52 weeks while the broad dollar has already slipped 1% over the month; crowded positioning adds to downside skew for DTWEXBGS.

Rising AFE sovereign yields and a shift from price-insensitive official holders to private buyers of Treasuries support global term premium: slight upward pressure on US 10y and a steeper 2s10s, little effect on the Fed-anchored 2y.

Foreign growth is soft (euro area, Canada, Mexico weak; Europe and lower-income Asia hit by energy costs) while high-tech Asia booms on AI; net modestly negative for oil demand, roughly neutral for US equities, with a weaker dollar offsetting softer external demand.
A softer dollar gives gold a small tailwind; credit spreads, breakevens and VIX get little directional signal from the global factor.

WTI at $86 sits well above pre-conflict levels after a +22% July spike and a -6% pullback last week; the price still carries a geopolitical (Hormuz) risk premium that tends to bleed out, and a backwardated curve implies downward spot drift absent new disruptions.

Fed staff expect retail gasoline to decline in H2; a Hormuz agreement was already reached in June, and the July re-spike looks partly reversible. Speculative CL longs rose +38k, leaving some room for liquidation.
Risk is two-sided: the conflict is ongoing and tail spikes are large (1y range $55-115), so the downside tilt on oil is only modest.

Pass-through: lower energy implies softer headline inflation and breakevens and slightly lower front-end and 10y yields, with a mild tailwind for equities; the effect on the curve, the dollar, HY spreads, and VIX is roughly neutral.
Gold has decoupled from energy (down 14% in 3m while oil swung), so this factor gives no clear signal for gold.

Middle East conflict and the Strait of Hormuz remain the dominant geopolitical driver. The June US-Iran memorandum crushed the oil risk premium, but WTI then rebounded 22% in July before falling 6% last week. That points to a fragile, two-sided situation.

With WTI at $86, still well above the post-deal lows near $55, some risk premium remains in the price. If the agreement holds, that premium tends to decay, so I lean slightly lower on oil and breakevens. Re-escalation is the fat upside tail.

VIX sits at about 16 (23rd percentile) and HY spreads are tight, which leaves little geopolitical risk priced. Shocks are asymmetric and the US midterm campaign heats up into October, so I tilt slightly toward higher VIX and wider spreads.
Gold is near one-year lows after the peace-driven unwind, which makes it cheap as a hedge against renewed conflict or election and tariff uncertainty. I take a mild upside tilt.

Risk-off episodes would pull Treasury yields slightly lower and support the dollar, but the effect is small next to the policy and inflation drivers. I hold rates near neutral with a marginal steepening bias from term-premium and fiscal-politics risk.

thesis:
The Fed has turned hawkish. It held in July with three dissents for a hike, it dropped the easing bias, and its minutes show 'many' participants seeing rates above the current range by year-end. Growth is running hot: GDPNow is about 5% and claims are 197k. Core PCE is about 3.3%. Together these tilt yields up.

The growth, inflation, labor and policy views share one hawkish driver, so I shrink the pooled log-odds sharply. Yields are also already at 1y highs, specs are short 10y futures, and the 2y is priced about 65bp over the funds rate.

The 10y gets a slightly larger and more durable tilt than the 2y, from term premium, refunding supply and a shift toward price-sensitive holders. That gives a mild 2s10s steepening bias at 3m.

The dollar leans lower: DX positioning is crowded long at the 99th percentile and foreign central banks are hiking.

Oil leans lower as the Hormuz risk premium decays after the July spike, but tail risk keeps the tilt modest. Gold gets a mild contrarian lift from washed-out positioning near 1y lows plus hedge demand.

Equities keep their positive drift, trimmed by rate headwinds and crowded ES positioning. VIX at the 23rd percentile, tight HY spreads, private-credit strains and the Aug–Oct seasonal window tilt volatility and spreads modestly higher.

Breakevens are near neutral: an energy rebound in the July prints is offset by premium decay and Fed credibility.
